dedupe_keys.name: techno economic cost framework for leo satellite broadband starlink oneweb and kuiper assessment

description: This paper presents an open-source techno-economic framework for satellite broadband, motivated by the lack of open modelling of satellite connectivity. A generalisable model assesses the engineering economics of a constellation, and is applied to Starlink, OneWeb and Kuiper by simulating coverage, capacity and cost as satellite numbers and subscribers grow, followed by a global assessment of capacity and cost per user. Results show that capacity thins quickly: at one user per 10 km2 the mean busy-hour capacity per user is 24.94, 1.01 and 10.30 Mbps for Starlink, OneWeb and Kuiper, falling to 2.49, 0.10 and 1.02 Mbps at one user per km2, and the authors conclude that mega-constellations most likely need to operate below 0.1 users per km2 to outcompete other broadband options. Producer: Osoro B. Ogutu and Edward J. Oughton; the arXiv abstract page shows a submission on 24 August 2021 (14 pages, six figures, submitted to IEEE Access). Coverage: global, for three named constellations. Access: free PDF and HTML on arXiv; the abstract states the codebase is open source, but no repository link was read here. Licence and cost: free to read; the code licence is not confirmed, and the paper is under the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence. Caveats: results depend on the published constellation parameters and assumed subscriber scenarios of 2021. Simulation uses: it supports capacity planning and cost comparison of satellite broadband for unserved areas. Related records: the Universal Techno-Economic Model (model-utem-universal-techno-economic-model) and the raw Starlink and OneWeb monitoring data (data-raw-starlink-and-oneweb-monitoring-data).
